question: What flat late-time background profiles fit the paired 13-entry DESI DR2 BAO Gaussian likelihood?
hypothesis: One free ruler-amplitude parameter suffices for a transparent BAO-only shape comparison; the resulting minima are screening fits, not collaboration posteriors.
assumptions_and_units: Flat late-time matter plus dark energy; radiation and curvature omitted.
alpha=c/(H0 rd) is dimensionless and free, so H0 and rd are not separated.
All 13 released measurements are distances divided by rd; full covariance retained in released row order.

nuisance_parameters.alpha: free c/(H0 rd) amplitude profiled by optimizer; no calibrated rd or H0

training_validation_holdout_definition: No training split or holdout; all 13 compressed BAO entries enter the correlated Gaussian likelihood.
covariance_order_and_overlap_treatment: Use full released 13x13 covariance in desi_dr2_mean.txt row order, including high-z DH then DM. No additional probe is multiplied.

numerical_checks.radiation_check: fixed-parameter illustrative Omega_r=9e-5 sensitivity only; no refit; see results and separate radiation lane

metric_definition: Minimum residual^T C^-1 residual with full Gaussian covariance; profile-chi-square differences are descriptive only.
uncertainty: No posterior uncertainty or model-selection penalty calculated; local screening result only.
interpretation_and_limits: Baseline is reproduced numerically under its stated simplified late-time model. CPL reaches a w0 boundary; a lower minimum is not evidence of evolving dark energy. The radiation term is omitted and is under separate sensitivity review.
independent_reviewer: Independent scalar quadrature/full-covariance objective coded in scripts/run_seed_screen.py; later GPU scalar check independently validates the forward model.
review_disposition: Reproduced as an explicitly exploratory profile calculation; not an official DESI posterior reproduction.
next_test: Complete standard-radiation sensitivity screen tied to H0, and preserve the null-mock calibration for model-search interpretation.
